curriculum.targetTransformation: Build shoulders and chest that actually show

lessons.title: Master the flat press and dumbbell fly to load your chest from two angles
lessons.summary: Learners perform the Flat Bench Dumbbell Press and Dumbbell Flyes — the two foundational free-weight chest movements — learning proper set and rep structure before adding machines or cables.

sessions.title: Flat Bench Dumbbell Press and Dumbbell Flyes
sessions.summary: Two foundational free-weight chest exercises performed for 3 sets of 10 reps each with 60-second rest periods — establishing the pressing and fly movement patterns that underpin every lesson ahead.

steps.title: Perform the Flat Bench Dumbbell Press and Dumbbell Flyes exactly as demonstrated
Reflect on the difference between pressing and flying as chest movements

clips.chapterTitle: Flat Bench Dumbbell Press — 3 sets of 10

lessons.title: Hit your chest from every angle using machines and cables in one complete session
lessons.summary: Learners work through four machine and cable chest exercises — Machine Chest Press, Low Pulley Cable Fly, Machine Chest Fly, and Decline Cable Crossover — building on the free-weight foundation with guided-path and constant-tension variations.

sessions.title: Machine Chest Press, Cable Fly, Machine Chest Fly, and Decline Cable Crossover
sessions.summary: A 17-minute machine and cable chest circuit covering all four exercises from Video B's chest section — each performed for 3 sets of 10 reps with 60-second rest periods — providing constant tension and guided movement paths that complement the free-weight work from Lesson 1.

steps.title: Complete all four machine and cable chest exercises in sequence
Reflect on how machine and cable exercises compare to free-weight work

clips.chapterTitle: Machine Chest Press, Low Pulley Cable Fly, Machine Chest Fly, and Decline Cable Crossover — 3×10 each

lessons.title: Finish your chest session with bodyweight push-ups and decline cable crossovers
lessons.summary: Learners complete the chest portion of the Workout A routine with Bench Push-Ups and Decline Cable Crossover — two finishing movements that combine bodyweight endurance with cable-tension detail work to fully exhaust the chest.

sessions.title: Bench Push-Ups and Decline Cable Crossover as Chest Finishers
sessions.summary: The final two exercises of the Chest and Triceps A workout — Bench Push-Ups and Decline Cable Crossover — each performed for 3 sets of 10 reps with 60-second rests. These movements serve as finishers after heavier pressing and fly work, adding bodyweight endurance and cable detail to cap the chest session.

steps.title: Perform Bench Push-Ups and Decline Cable Crossover as a finishing superset
Reflect on where the Bench Push-Up and Decline Cable Crossover fit in a full chest session

clips.chapterTitle: Bench Push-Ups and Decline Cable Crossover — Chest Finishers, 3×10 each

lessons.title: Isolate and exhaust your triceps with bench dips and cable rope pushdowns
lessons.summary: Learners complete the triceps section of the Workout B routine — Triceps Bench Dips and Cable Rope Pushdown — performed after a full chest session, building the elbow-extension strength and muscle detail that makes pressed movements stronger and upper arms more defined.

sessions.title: Triceps Bench Dips and Cable Rope Pushdown
sessions.summary: The complete triceps block from Workout B — Triceps Bench Dips and Cable Rope Pushdown — each for 3 sets of 10 reps with 60-second rests. Performed after a full chest session, these two exercises isolate the triceps through bodyweight dipping and cable extension patterns to finish the upper-body training cycle.

steps.title: Perform Triceps Bench Dips and Cable Rope Pushdown back-to-back after your chest work
Reflect on how training triceps after chest changes the effort required
